One photograph, five findings

Upload a fundus or OCT image and get a read on the five markers of diabetic retinopathy. Each finding comes with a confidence score, a plain description and its own heatmap, so the doctor can see where the model looked.

Traditional
Manual grading, delayed, single reader
Vision Quest
AI triage, heatmaps and a doctor queue
Output
7-page PDF: patient details, 5 conditions, 1 summary

Built for PHCs, rural centres and district hospitals. Works offline with the embedded demo images on any device.

  • MicroaneurysmsTiny swellings in retinal capillaries, often the earliest sign of retinopathy.
  • HemorrhagesBleeding inside the retina from weakened vessels.
  • ExudatesYellow fatty deposits left behind by leaking vessels.
  • Cotton-wool spotsPale patches where blood flow to the nerve fibre layer is blocked.
  • NeovascularizationFragile new vessels that signal advanced, proliferative disease.

How a screening flows

Seven steps from registration to a signed report. The first three happen at the health centre; the rest are handled remotely.

Doctor and report

  2. 5ReviewDoctor panel

  4. 7PDF report7 pages

All AI outputs are assistive. Final interpretation rests with a licensed ophthalmologist. This is a prototype for demonstration.

How the queue works (Gov. workflow)

1. Rural Centre Submits
Case enters queue with Patient ID, Case ID, timestamp and image reference.
2. Auto-Triage (~10s)
Demo automation decides Accept vs Overwrite. In production this is manual by the duty ophthalmologist.
3. Doctor Review
Accepted cases appear in the Doctor Review Panel with AI findings, heatmaps and clinical actions.
